title: Fatimah's last months
hookLine: the Prophet's daughter dies within months of her father, and her grief is remembered by Sunni and Shia Muslims alike

lines: A SECOND WHISPER, AND SHE LAUGHS.
cards: A sick room in Medina. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is in his last illness, and his daughter Fatimah comes in. Aisha, who is there, later says that Fatimah walked exactly the way her father walked.
He welcomes her and sits her beside him. Then he leans in and whispers something, and Fatimah cries. He whispers a second time, and she laughs.
Aisha asks her what he said. Fatimah won't tell, not until after he has died. Today, the months that came after that whisper.

teach.h: THE FIRST WHISPER: HE WOULD DIE.
teach.b: When Aisha asks again, after the Prophet's death, Fatimah tells her. The first whisper: he would die of this illness. So she cried.

teach.h: THE SECOND: SHE WOULD FOLLOW HIM FIRST.
teach.b: The second: she would be the first of his household to follow him. So she laughed. The news of her own death made her laugh.
Bukhari and Muslim both record it, and in the same report he tells her she will be a leader among the women of Paradise. Then the days of grief.
As his illness grew heavy, Bukhari records, Fatimah said, oh, the pain my father is in. And he answered her gently: there will be no more pain for your father after today.
When he died, she called him again and again: oh my father.

teach.h: HOW COULD YOU POUR EARTH ON HIM?
teach.b: And after the burial she turned to Anas and asked how they could bring themselves to pour earth over the Messenger of God. There is no theory in that question: it is a daughter at a grave.
In those same months, Bukhari also records, Fatimah asked Abu Bakr for her share of what her father had left, and he answered with a saying of the Prophet that prophets leave no inheritance.
Sunni and Shia Muslims read that exchange very differently, and both traditions remember her grief.

teach.h: NO MORE PAIN FOR YOUR FATHER AFTER TODAY.
teach.b: The same report says she lived on for months after her father, not years. She followed him soon, as the second whisper had said.
Shia Muslims honor her among the Ma'sumin, those they hold were kept free of sin; Sunni Muslims honor her as the Prophet's beloved daughter and a leader of the women of Paradise. Different words.
The same tears at the same grave.

how: Sunni and Shia Muslims both honor Fatimah as the Prophet's daughter; Sunnis usually follow her name with 'may God be pleased with her' and Shia Muslims with 'peace be upon her', and her life and grief are retold in sermons and gatherings.

o: the Prophet's daughter, first of his household to follow him
the Prophet's nurse, who cared for him as a baby
the Prophet's wife who nursed him in his last illness

games.q: Fatimah's last months — tap the pairs.
p: he would die of this illness
oh, the pain my father is in
how could you pour earth on him?

s: Fatimah laughed at the second whisper because he would recover
she laughed because he told her she would be the first of his household to follow him.
Fatimah told Aisha the secret right away
she kept it until after the Prophet had died.
the report says she lived months, not years, after her father
Bukhari's report says she lived on for months after him.

games.q: you are Fatimah. your father has whispered twice, and you cried and then laughed. Aisha asks what he said. what do you do?
o: keep it to yourself until after he has died.
games.why: she kept the secret while he lived. only after his death did she tell Aisha: he would die, and she would be first of his household to follow.

practice: Picture the room: a dying father, a daughter beside him, two whispers. If you pray, ask peace and mercy for her in your own words; Sunni Muslims often say, may God be pleased with her, and Shia Muslims often say, peace be upon her.
If you don't pray, hold her name, and the name of someone you've lost.

wordCard.voice: Fatimah. The Prophet's daughter, told in a whisper that she would be the first of his household to follow him, and who did, after only months of grief. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the name of the Prophet's daughter, honored in both Sunni and Shia tradition.

carryVoice: Your line: she followed him soon. The second whisper was a comfort. Day eight hundred sixty-seven.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3623–3624; Sahih Muslim 2450 (the two whispers; first of his household to follow him; leader of the women of Paradise)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4462 (oh, the pain my father is in; no pain after today; her words at his death and to Anas)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4240–4241 (Fatimah asks Abu Bakr for her share; she lived months after the Prophet)
